For a≠0 the pushforward has density equal to the section area divided by |a|, so it has no atom at zero. Its section-area profile is bounded and compactly supported. Translating the sections to a common copy of a⊥ makes the Brunn–Minkowski argument valid; central symmetry gives equal endpoint areas. The m=1 interval has a constant marginal.

For p=m+1 the test denominator from ffcc7a246184e668 is admissible at every point of A, including the cutting plane. When m≥2 and v<1, the strict pointwise comparison with exponent two applies off the marginal-null height zero on a captured set of positive mass, giving strictness before taking the infimum.

A and −A cover D, so their intersection has volume (2v−1)|D| and is a centrally symmetric convex body containing a neighborhood of zero. The stated accepted fact gives its energy equal to its volume and monotonicity gives the lower bound.

The lower ratio reduces to v²/(3v−1); the exact difference from 4/9 is (3v−2)²/[9(3v−1)]. The lower energy bound gives the upper ratio 1/2. For A=D both energy bounds give one after normalization. On [−1,1/3] the maximizing quadratic parameter is ℓ=−1, admissible on both endpoints; the energy is 1, so v=2/3 gives ratio 4/9.
